newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss Life group profit rises, Q1 strong.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Life group profit rises, Q1 strong.

text.p: Swiss Life/Rentenanstalt, the Swiss mutual insurer which has proposed converting into a public limited company pending shareholder approval, said its 1996 group profit rose to 1.509 billion Swiss francs from 1.309 billion in 1995.
It also said that the first quarter developed well, and that it saw an increase in premiums of over 10 percent.
"One can speak of an all-round gratifying first quarter," said Manfred Zobl, said chairman of Swiss Life's corporate executive board in a text.
Premium income rose by over 10 percent in the first quarter, the firm said.
Both individual and corporate business showed positive results.
Swiss Life also benefited from favourable financial markets, realising profits from share holdings.
At the same time, Zobl said that the current low level of bond yields in Switzerland were a cause for concern.

Swiss Life already said it will ask its roughly 600,000 members to vote on management's proposal to turn the company into a public company. The voting period is from May 26 to June 20. If approved, Swiss Life will be listed on the Swiss Exchange on July 3. -- Zurich Editorial, +41 1 63 7340
